**Visual observations:**
- Young soybean seedlings at very early growth stage (cotyledon/first trifoliate stage)
- Plants are severely wilted and collapsing — stems appear pinched/constricted at or near the soil line
- Leaves are yellowed, brown, shriveled, and dying
- Sandy soil visible
- Multiple seedlings affected in close proximity
- No visible leaf spots or lesions — the damage is a whole-plant damping-off pattern
- Stems appear thin and constricted near the soil surface (classic "wire stem" or pre/post-emergence damping-off)

**Reasoning:**
- The pattern of young seedling collapse with stem constriction at the soil line is the hallmark of **damping-off** diseases
- The sandy, well-drained-looking soil and the seedling stage points strongly to Pythium damping-off (favors wet/poorly-drained conditions but also sandy soils with moisture fluctuations) OR Rhizoctonia (also causes damping-off)
- Pythium damping-off: pre- and post-emergence damping-off, water-soaked lesions, rapid collapse, seedlings look "melted" near soil line
- Rhizoctonia: post-emergence damping-off, reddish-brown sunken lesion on hypocotyl ("wire stem"), plants can stand briefly then fall
- The plants here show severe wilting with the stem still somewhat intact but clearly constricted — this "wire stem" appearance with multiple collapsed seedlings is very characteristic of **Pythium damping-off**
- The overall seedling death with no leaf spotting, occurring at cotyledon/very early stage in sandy soil is most consistent with Pythium damping-off
